final:
I checked all 19 review issues against the code and wrote the verdicts to `verdicts.json`. No code was changed and no replies were posted. One limit: `zod` isn't installed here, so I worked out the schema behaviour in #5 by reading the code rather than running it.

## Summary

| Verdict | Count | IDs |
|---|---|---|
| VALID, should be fixed | 11 | 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 12, 13, 14, 17, 18, plus 5 (below) |
| VALID, optional | 2 | 0, 10 |
| PARTIALLY_VALID, should be fixed | 1 | 5 |
| PARTIALLY_VALID, optional | 3 | 9, 11, 15 |
| INVALID | 3 | 2, 8, 16 |

## Most serious real bugs
- **#18, Google Calendar:** at `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97`, the whole `{success, data}` result object is saved as the credential key instead of just the tokens. The next time the credential loads, the schema check at `:75` fails, so the Google credential is broken after its first refresh.
- **#7 / #14, wrong response shape:** when credential sync is on, `refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15` returns a raw `fetch` Response. Google, Zoho Bigin, Zoho CRM and HubSpot expect something with a `.data` property (or a HubSpot token object), so they crash. The `() => any` typing (#10) is why this compiles without errors.
- **#12, Salesforce:** `salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96` uses `prisma` but never imports it.
- **#17, Salesforce:** the connection is built with the old `access_token` and `instance_url` instead of the newly refreshed ones.
- **#13, Zoho Bigin:** it sends the credential id to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`, so the sync targets the wrong user.
- **#6, lost refresh tokens:** a placeholder `"refresh_token"` string overwrites the real Office 365 refresh token.

## Where the reviewer was partly right or wrong
- **#5:** the schema is broken, but not the way they said. Both computed keys become the literal string `"[object Object]"`, and the second (optional) one overwrites the first, so nothing extra is required. The real problem is that zod drops unknown keys by default, so `expires_in` and `refresh_token` are lost. That is also what makes #6 hit every time sync is on.
- **#2:** a repeated or array-valued header fails the strict `!==` check, so the request is rejected, not let through.
- **#8:** a failed `fetch` is passed up to the caller exactly as the provider calls did before this PR, so nothing changed.
- **#16:** `parseRefreshTokenResponse` now throws when parsing fails, so the database update is never reached. Nothing stale gets saved.

## Webhook endpoint
- **#3 / #4 are valid:** the body parse and the decrypt/`JSON.parse` step have no error handling, so bad input returns a 500 instead of a 400.
- **#1 is valid:** Node lowercases incoming header names, so if the header-name setting has any capitals, every request is rejected.
- **#15 is plausible but unlikely:** two simultaneous requests could create duplicate credentials, because there's no unique constraint on user and app.
